projects.name: Ask the Multiverse - cited Marvel multiverse Q&A
projects.description: Ask the Multiverse: ask anything about the multiverse. Every answer cites its sources. An unofficial, fan-made explorer and Q&A bot over a knowledge graph built from the Marvel Database and MCU Wiki (Fandom, CC BY-SA) and Wikidata (CC0). An LLM (Groq gpt-oss-120b, Gemini fallback, rule-based planner without keys) turns a question into a typed graph query or a guarded read-only DuckDB SELECT; the answer is built only from the returned rows, shows the query it ran, and links to the exact wiki pages and revisions used. Built with FastAPI, DuckDB and React. Fan-made project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Marvel or Disney.
highlights: Grounded answers: every answer is built only from query rows and cites the wiki pages and revisions it used; if the data can't answer, it says so.
LLM to typed tools or guarded SQL: 18 typed query tools, plus model-written SQL that must be a single read-only SELECT on whitelisted tables, capped at 200 rows and 3 seconds.
Evaluation set: 80 questions with expected plans and answer facts, scoring 100% plan and answer accuracy with both the rule planner and the LLM planner.
"Who fought whom" from story roles: opposite sides of the same story (antagonist vs. featured or supporting), never mentions or visions, across 985k appearances.

Honest data pipeline: polite MediaWiki API ingest (1 request/s, cached, resumable), infobox-based classification, quality checks that block publishing, and a Coverage page listing every rejected or unlinked page.

Production: Firebase Hosting + Cloud Run (scale to zero) + GCS snapshots, keyless Workload Identity Federation, approval-gated deploys, and a weekly data sync that publishes only when every check passes.

case_study.problem: Fan wikis hold huge, structured knowledge about the multiverse, but chatbots answer from memory and invent facts. I wanted an LLM that works over structured data and shows its work.
approach: Knowledge-graph ETL from the wiki APIs: polite MediaWiki API ingest of the Marvel Database and MCU Wiki plus Wikidata, with infobox-based classification and quality checks that block publishing.
Typed tools plus guarded SQL: 18 typed query tools, and model-written SQL limited to a single read-only SELECT on whitelisted tables, capped at 200 rows and 3 seconds.
Answers built only from the returned rows, showing the query that ran and citing the exact wiki pages and revisions used.
An evaluation set of 80 questions with expected plans and answer facts that scores both plans and answers.

decisions.title: Answers only from returned rows
decisions.detail: The LLM never answers from memory. It plans a typed graph query or a guarded DuckDB SELECT, the answer is built only from the rows that come back, and when the data can't answer the question, the app says so.

decisions.title: Typed tools first, guarded SQL second
decisions.detail: 18 typed query tools cover common questions. Model-written SQL is allowed only as a single read-only SELECT on whitelisted tables, capped at 200 rows and 3 seconds. Groq gpt-oss-120b plans, Gemini is the fallback, and a rule-based planner works without keys.

decisions.title: "Who fought whom" from story roles
decisions.detail: Fights come from characters on opposite sides of the same story (antagonist vs. featured or supporting), never from mentions or visions.

challenges: Resolving names across 5,531 realities, dimensions and realms and 8,030 variant groups.
Deriving opponents from story roles across 985,849 story appearances without counting mentions or visions.
Ingesting the wiki APIs politely (1 request/s, cached, resumable) while listing every rejected or unlinked page on a Coverage page.
case_study.outcome: A live explorer at multiverse.arunangshupramanik.com. The latest sync holds 5,531 realities, dimensions and realms, 106,838 characters (with origin, powers, deaths), 12,142 teams, 387 events, 77,880 stories, 985,849 story appearances with roles, 169,249 sourced relationships, 8,030 variant groups, and an MCU timeline with 6 phases and all 71 titles linked. The 80-question evaluation set scores 100% plan and answer accuracy with both the rule planner and the LLM planner. Fan-made project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Marvel or Disney.

projects.name: Flowbench - data pipeline playground
projects.description: Flowbench: build a pipeline, break it, inspect every row. An interactive data pipeline playground that runs real validation and transformation pipelines on seeded datasets, compiles them to DuckDB SQL, and lets you open every stage: records in and out, rejections with reasons, and record-level lineage. Built with FastAPI and React.
highlights: Typed pipeline builder: every validator and transform has a schema-aware editor with field pickers limited to the fields that exist at that stage.
Static planning before execution: the planner propagates the schema through each stage and reports errors and warnings; the API refuses to run a pipeline that has errors.
Real, bounded execution: rows stream lazily through stage iterators with exact, conserved counts (in = out + rejected + filtered) and per-stage timing.
Stage-level inspection: sampled input, output, and rejected records, a per-field profile over all rows, and schema in vs. out for every node.
Record-level lineage: every source row carries an ID you can trace through the stages, reporting honestly when a trace is not possible.

Failure to fix to replay to compare: a deliberately faulty dataset demonstrates rejection handling, replay-with-edits that links back to the original run, and run comparison that tolerates added or removed stages.

case_study.problem: Portfolio data projects usually show a static dashboard. I wanted to demonstrate real data-engineering judgment: pipeline design, validation, observability, and failure recovery as something a visitor can interact with, not read about.
approach: A whitelisted catalog of validators and transforms with typed parameter editors, so pipelines are configured, never scripted.
A static planner that propagates schemas through each stage before execution, catching bad params and missing fields without touching data.
Bounded in-process execution that streams rows lazily through stage iterators, with exact conserved counts and per-stage timing.
An inspection layer over an SVG pipeline graph: sampled records, rejections with reasons, per-field profiles, and lineage tracing per source row.

decisions.title: Whitelisted operations over arbitrary SQL/Python
decisions.detail: A public demo cannot execute visitor code safely. A fixed catalog of validators and transforms keeps the surface abuse-resistant while still covering the stages a real pipeline needs.

decisions.title: Plan-then-run over run-and-fail
decisions.detail: The planner catches schema errors statically and the API refuses to run pipelines that have them, so failures during execution are meaningful data failures, not typos.

decisions.title: Honest inspection over polished output
decisions.detail: Lineage traces report 'cannot tell' when a record is not in the recorded samples rather than guessing; counts are exact and conserved so the numbers can actually be trusted.

challenges: Propagating schemas through renames, drops, casts, and lookup joins so the planner's view of the data stays correct at every stage.
Aligning stages by operation when comparing two runs, so added or removed stages do not misalign the rest of the comparison.
Keeping a lazy, bounded execution model that still produces exact per-stage counts, timing, and full-dataset field profiles.
case_study.outcome: A live playground at flowbench.arunangshupramanik.com where visitors assemble pipelines from typed operations, run them on seeded datasets, inspect every stage and rejection, and demonstrate failure handling through a faulty-data demo with replay and run comparison.

projects.name: doppel - Mock API playground
projects.description: doppel: your backend stand-in. A schema-driven mock REST API generator that turns a JSON schema into a working API with realistic seeded data, resource relationships, and an interactive playground. Built with FastAPI, React, and Faker.
highlights: Define resources, field types, and ref() foreign-key links in JSON, then generate reproducible data from a fixed seed.
Typed generators for uuid, person, email, date, datetime, money, enums, sentences, and more across five locales.
Dynamic REST endpoints with pagination, exact-match filtering, sorting, and per-dataset OpenAPI docs.
Interactive playground with Table and JSON views, cURL copying, starter templates, and schema import/export.
Isolated read-only public demo and per-user playgrounds on Cloud Run and Firebase Hosting, with bounded request simulation and CI-gated keyless deploys.

case_study.problem: Frontend and QA work routinely stalls waiting for a real backend. Existing fake-API tools return placeholder gibberish, lack relationships between resources, and cannot reproduce the same dataset twice.
approach: A schema language in plain JSON: resources, field types, row counts, constraints, and ref() links between resources.
A deterministic generator built on Faker so the same seed always produces the same dataset, across five locales.
Dynamic FastAPI routes per dataset with pagination, exact-match filtering, sorting, and auto-generated OpenAPI docs.
A React playground with a schema editor, Table/JSON response explorer, cURL copying, and starter templates.

decisions.title: Seeded generation over random-on-request
decisions.detail: Deterministic output means two developers, or a developer and a CI run, see identical data. The seed lives in the schema itself, so sharing a schema reproduces an exact API.

decisions.title: Isolated playgrounds, no accounts
decisions.detail: Generating an API creates an isolated per-user playground instead of requiring sign-up, keeping the demo zero-friction. A read-only public demo gives visitors instant access while bounding abuse.

decisions.title: Bounded request simulation
decisions.detail: Optional delay, HTTP error, and empty-list simulation let developers test loading and failure states against the mock before pointing the same code at production.

challenges: Resolving ref() relationships so foreign keys always point at rows that actually exist, regardless of generation order.
Validating user schemas safely in a public app without executing arbitrary input.
Keeping the workbench drafts (imports, template and locale changes) from clobbering a working API until generation succeeds.
case_study.outcome: A public tool at doppel.arunangshupramanik.com that turns a JSON schema into a realistic, relational, reproducible REST API in seconds, deployed keylessly to Cloud Run and Firebase Hosting in its own GCP project.

projects.name: M.A.H.A.K.A.L.
projects.description: M.A.H.A.K.A.L.: Modular Agentic Hub for Automation, Knowledge & Adaptive Logic. A personal voice AI assistant built with FastAPI and React, powered by Groq (GPT-OSS 120B + Whisper) with Gemini fallback, plus Edge TTS.
highlights: Voice and text conversations with streamed responses, Whisper speech recognition, and Edge TTS playback.
Automatic Gemini fallback when the primary Groq provider fails or reaches its rate limit.
Google sign-in with guest-to-user conversation migration, persistent Firestore history, and long-term memory.
Tool calling for weather, time, Wikipedia lookup, and remembering or forgetting user preferences.
Cloud Run and Firebase Hosting deployment with Secret Manager, keyless GitHub authentication, and CI-gated releases.

case_study.problem: Personal AI assistants usually live behind closed products. I wanted a JARVIS-style assistant I fully controlled: voice-first, with persistent memory, tool calling, and a provider setup that would not fall over when a free-tier LLM hit its rate limit.
approach: FastAPI backend orchestrating LLM calls, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and tool execution behind a single streaming endpoint.
React + Vite frontend with a sci-fi HUD, live diagnostics, streaming replies, and a music player.
Firestore for conversation history and long-term memory, keyed by Google sign-in or a guest identity.
Keyless GitHub Actions pipeline deploying to Cloud Run and Firebase Hosting in a dedicated GCP project.

decisions.title: Groq primary with Gemini fallback
decisions.detail: Groq gives near-instant inference on GPT-OSS 120B and hosted Whisper, but free-tier limits are real. Every LLM call wraps the primary provider and falls back to Gemini on failure or rate limiting, so the assistant keeps answering instead of erroring.

decisions.title: Guest sessions that migrate on sign-in
decisions.detail: Letting people try the assistant before signing in improves the demo. Guests get a message budget; when they authenticate with Google, their Firestore conversation history is migrated to the permanent identity rather than discarded.

decisions.title: Firestore over a relational store
decisions.detail: Conversation and memory documents are write-simple and read-heavy with no joins, so a document database keeps the data layer at zero operational cost on the free tier.

challenges: Streaming voice replies while keeping Whisper transcription latency low required careful chunking of STT, LLM, and TTS stages.
Merging guest history into an authenticated account without duplicating or reordering messages.
Keeping a fully themed HUD responsive on mobile while the diagnostics panels animate.
case_study.outcome: A live, publicly accessible assistant at mahakal.arunangshupramanik.com that handles voice and text, remembers preferences across sessions, calls tools for weather, time and Wikipedia, and ships through a fully keyless CI/CD pipeline.
